sections.h2: Where is Rock Hill, and which county handles its property tax?
sections.html:
Rock Hill is in York County, South Carolina, and York County offices assess and bill the tax on a Rock Hill house. The city sits in the north-central Piedmont on the Catawba River, about 25 miles south of Charlotte and about 70 miles north of Columbia.

The city covers 43.85 square miles, and its northern edge reaches Lake Wylie. The 2020 census counted 74,372 residents, which made Rock Hill the largest city in York County and the fifth-largest in the state. The Census Bureau's 2025 estimate is 75,911.

York County itself was formed in 1785, has its seat in the town of York, and covers about 682 square miles of land. The 2020 census put the county at 282,090 people, seventh in the state. Rock Hill shares the county with Fort Mill, Tega Cay, Clover, Lake Wylie and several smaller towns, so a tax question about a Rock Hill parcel goes to the county, not to a neighboring town.

sections.h2: What shaped Rock Hill's housing and tax base?
sections.html:
The railroad started the city. The first passenger train arrived on March 23, 1852, and the town took its name from a rocky hill near the tracks. Textile mills later drove growth, and when that work moved overseas the city had to find other employers.

Today the list of top employers includes 3D Systems, Comporium Communications, Hyosung, Winthrop University, Rock Hill Schools and the City of Rock Hill. Winthrop was founded in 1886, Clinton College in 1894 and York Technical College in 1964, and the university and school payrolls are part of the local job base.

Public schools belong to York County School District 3, which runs 27 schools. Rock Hill High School, Northwestern High School and South Pointe High School are its high schools.

sections.h2: How does South Carolina decide what you owe on a Rock Hill house?
sections.html:
The tax starts with an appraised value multiplied by an assessment ratio, and the ratio depends on how the house is used. Under state Department of Revenue guidance, an owner-occupied primary residence is assessed at 4 percent. A second home, vacant land and commercial property are assessed at 6 percent.

The 4 percent ratio is not automatic. The owner applies to the county assessor before the first penalty date, which is January 16, and certifies that the home is the legal residence and that no other home carries the 4 percent rate.

  • A buyer who moves in within 90 days of closing can get the 4 percent ratio back to the purchase date.
  • Renting the home for more than 72 days in the tax year can disqualify it, so landlords should ask the assessor before relying on the lower ratio.
  • A sale counts as an assessable transfer of interest, which means the parcel is reappraised, and the 15 percent cap on increases does not apply in the first year after that transfer.

That last point matters when you price a Rock Hill house. A buyer's first bill can be higher than yours was.

sections.h2: When is Rock Hill property tax due, and what do late payments cost?
sections.html:
State law makes taxes payable between September 30 and January 15. Penalties start the next day, in three steps.

  • 3 percent is added starting January 16.
  • A further 7 percent is added after the second day of February.
  • A further 5 percent is added after March 17, which brings the total to 15 percent of the original bill.

After that the county treasurer can issue a tax execution, and collection continues under the state's delinquent tax chapter. The statute also requires penalties to be waived in certain title transfers when the new owner received no timely notice. If a closing is close to January, ask the closing attorney whether that waiver could apply.

State law also describes an installment plan with five payments on February 15, April 15, June 15, August 15 and October 15, with an election due by January 15.

sections.h2: How do you challenge a Rock Hill assessment?
sections.html:
You object in writing within 90 days after the assessor mails the assessment notice. Once you do, each later step has its own clock, and missing one can end the appeal.

  1. Ask for a meeting with the assessor in the same 90-day window. The assessor must schedule it within 30 days, or as soon after as practical.
  2. File a written protest within 30 days after that conference. The assessor answers by mail, usually within another 30 days.
  3. Appeal to the York County Board of Assessment Appeals within 30 days after the assessor's response.
  4. Ask for a contested case hearing before the state Administrative Law Court within 30 days after the board's written decision.

The county's board has seven seats and was created under 1968 state legislation. In years when no notice is mailed, state law lets you appeal at any time in writing, and a filing made before the first penalty date applies to that tax year.

sections.h2: What happens to the tax when a Rock Hill house is sold?
sections.html:
The tax follows the property, and the seller's share is usually settled from the sale proceeds at closing. State law gives the auditor a way to split a bill between the original owner and the new owner when a transfer comes after assessment.

In South Carolina, the closing itself must be supervised by a licensed South Carolina attorney. The State Bar says every stage of a real estate deal, including drafting documents, closing and recording, is the practice of law, so the attorney or title company you work with will run the tax proration and payoff.

Recording the deed carries a state fee of $1.85 for each $500 of the price, and counties keep $0.55 of that. Who pays it is set by the contract, so read that clause before you sign.

Owners who are 65 or older, totally disabled or legally blind may qualify for the state homestead exemption, which removes the first $50,000 of a home's value from county, school and city bills. You have to apply, so ask the assessor if it applies to your house before you sell.

sections.h2: Which Rock Hill code problems can follow a house to closing?
sections.html:
Overgrown grass, junk and parked vehicles are the usual ones, and the city's Neighborhood Inspections office enforces them. Grass or weeds over 12 inches on an improved lot, or 18 inches on a vacant lot, can bring a notice.

The first courtesy notice comes once a calendar year and gives 7 days for debris and grass or 15 days for vehicles. After that, tickets are issued every 7 days at $25, $50 and $100, up to $250. Unresolved cases can go to Environmental Court, which meets on the third Wednesday of the month at 120 East Black Street, with fines up to $1,087.50 or up to 30 days in jail.

If the city clears the lot, it bills the owner, and an unpaid bill becomes a lien on the property. A lien like that shows up in a title search and has to be paid before the sale closes. Call 803-329-7014 to ask about an open case. You do not have to give your name when you report a problem, but you should give it when you ask about your own address.

sections.h2: How do Rock Hill's roads and weather affect a sale?
sections.html:
Rock Hill is a short drive from Charlotte. Interstate 77 serves the city through exits 73 to 82, and Interstate 85 reaches it at exit 102. Charlotte Douglas International Airport is about 20 miles north.

The climate is humid subtropical. July highs average about 91 degrees and January highs about 51, with roughly 42.62 inches of precipitation a year. Cooling, roof and moisture problems tend to come up in a buyer's inspection, and a repair list can reshape a deal. A cash sale as-is avoids that back and forth.

faqs.q: Does the city of Rock Hill or York County send my property tax bill?
faqs.a: York County sends it. The county assessor sets the value and the county Tax Collection office bills and collects, as the offices on this page show. Call them for your parcel's current bill.

faqs.q: What is the last day to pay Rock Hill property tax without a penalty?
faqs.a: January 15. Under state law, a 3 percent penalty starts on January 16, another 7 percent after the second day of February, and another 5 percent after March 17.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal my Rock Hill assessment?
faqs.a: You have 90 days after the assessor mails the assessment notice to object in writing. Later steps, such as the protest and the board appeal, carry 30-day deadlines.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Rock Hill house if I still owe property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. The unpaid tax is deducted from your proceeds at closing, and the closing attorney handles the payoff. A city code lien must also be cleared.

faqs.q: Does a new owner keep my 4 percent tax rate?
faqs.a: No. A sale triggers a reappraisal, and the buyer must apply for the 4 percent rate. A buyer who moves in within 90 days can have it applied back to the purchase date.
